entries.title: Passing concepts stress space and defender rules
entries.summary: Route combinations are designed to stress particular defenders, zones, leverage or assignment rules; SAGE should analyze concepts as interacting routes rather than independent route labels.

entries.title: Yankee-style post/cross play-action stress
entries.summary: A post/deep-cross play-action concept can stress deep safety structure and use run action to influence defenders; the preferred throw changes with coverage response.
limitations: Terminology and coaching rules vary; do not assume every post-cross concept uses identical reads.

entries.title: Hank-style underneath zone stress
entries.summary: One documented Hank implementation uses underneath routes to stretch Cover 3 hook/curl-flat defenders and gives the quarterback movement keys based on those defenders.
limitations: This is a documented implementation, not a universal definition for every playbook.

entries.title: Route-concept versus coverage interaction can improve player opportunity forecasts
entries.summary: If SAGE knows a team's concept usage, a defense's rules, and a player's participation within those concepts, it may forecast targets/explosives more accurately than aggregate matchup statistics alone.
